how appropriability mechanisms affect the likelihood that a platform owner and an ISV will partner.
how appropriability mechanisms influence the platform partnership decisions of ISVs.

IPR is an effective means of appropriating the returns to platform innovation.
formal IPR and downstream capabilities are effective mechanisms for protecting ISVs from appropriation of returns by the platform owner.

formal IPR and downstream capabilities are effective mechanisms for appropriating the returns from innovation and for encouraging entry by independent firms into markets complementary to the proprietary technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the platform partnership decision is a function of both the appropriability mechanisms and the threat of imitation, and that IPR are more effective in protecting the returns from innovation in markets that are less attractive for imitation.

IPR and downstream capabilities can help ISVs to appropriate returns from innovation and protect them from the threat of imitation, and thus, these ISVs are more likely to enter into a partnership with a platform owner.
IPR and downstream capabilities are effective in encouraging entry by ISVs into markets complementary to the proprietary platform by protecting them from the platform owner’s expropriation.

the appropriability mechanisms that are available to ISVs are effective in encouraging entry, but that the effectiveness of these mechanisms depends on the ISV’s capabilities.
